steps.say: The palate is forming when two shelves rise and fuse in the midline. These secondary palatal shelves are growing from the maxillary prominences, and their fusion is failing between the eighth and twelfth weeks of gestation in cleft palate. The same failed fusion is producing the lip and palate clefting shown in syndromes such as EEC.
steps.tx: **Cleft palate** (an open gap in the roof of the mouth from failed midline fusion) results from failure of fusion of the **secondary palatal shelves** (paired maxillary outgrowths that rise above the tongue and meet centrally) derived from **maxillary prominences** (the upper jaw swellings of the embryonic face) between the **8th** and **12th** weeks of **gestation** (pregnancy counted from fertilisation). Syndromic clefting shows the same fusion failure.

vis.alt: Child with EEC syndrome showing cleft lip and palate from failed fusion of the facial prominences.
vis.caption: Orofacial clefting in EEC syndrome; isolated cleft palate reflects the same failed shelf fusion. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: The calendar is balancing speech against growth. Repair between nine and twelve months is giving the infant a working velum before babbling habits fix. Earlier closure is favouring speech while disturbing maxillary growth, and later closure is sparing growth while letting nasal speech harden.
steps.tx: Optimal timing for **cleft palate repair** (surgical closure restoring a functional velum) is between **9** and **12 months** of age, balancing **speech development** (babbling and articulation built on a sealed palate) needs against potential maxillary growth restriction. Operating in this window gives the child sealed anatomy just as canonical babbling begins.

rows: Working velum before speech patterns fix
Better babbling but more growth disturbance
Spares growth but speech habits harden

steps.say: The lifting muscle is anchored in the wrong place and is needing release. In clefts the levator veli palatini is inserting into the posterior hard palate margin as the Laimer bundle instead of forming a sling. The surgeon is dissecting it free and is swinging it back into a transverse muscular sling.
steps.tx: Abnormal insertion of the **levator veli palatini** (the muscle sling that lifts the soft palate during speech) into the posterior border of the hard palate cleft margin, the **Laimer muscle** (the misdirected levator bundle), must be dissected and **retropositioned** (released and reset backward) into a transverse **muscular sling**. Without this rebuild, the palate looks closed but speech stays nasal.

rows: Fibres run forward into the cleft margin
Laimer bundle tethers the margin instead

steps.say: The Furlow repair is lengthening the palate while rebuilding the sling. Mirrored Z-plasties are crossing on the two palate surfaces in opposite directions. The levator is riding into position on the flaps, and narrow clefts with supple tissue are responding best.
steps.tx: **Furlow double-reversing Z-plasty** (two mirror-image Z-plasties on opposite palate surfaces) transposes opposing mucoperiosteal and **myomucosal flaps** (mucosa plus muscle layers) across oral and nasal layers, **retropositioning** the levator muscle and lengthening the soft palate. The design suits narrow clefts; wide gaps need the two-flap route instead.

steps.say: Wide clefts are needing two robust flaps with named blood supply. Bilateral mucoperiosteal flaps are being raised on the greater palatine arteries and are meeting tension-free in the midline. Bardach two-flap palatoplasty is closing gaps that a Furlow cannot bridge.
steps.tx: **Two-flap palatoplasty** in the **Bardach** style (bilateral full-thickness palate flaps) provides complete tension-free oral closure by mobilising bilateral **mucoperiosteal flaps** (mucosa with underlying periosteum) based on the **greater palatine artery** (dominant hard-palate vessels feeding each side). **Two** large axial flaps bridge wide clefts that a Furlow cannot span.

rows: Raised off the hard palate shelves

steps.say: A leaking palate is betraying itself in speech. Hypernasality is colouring vowels, air is escaping through the nose on pressure consonants, and the child is developing compensatory articulation errors. Video nasoendoscopy is watching the velopharyngeal gap directly and is guiding the operation.
steps.tx: **Velopharyngeal insufficiency** (**VPI**, failed palate to back-wall seal during speech) presents with **hypernasality** (excess nasal resonance), **nasal air emission** (audible leak on pressure consonants), and **compensatory articulation errors** (glottal stops and backing), diagnosed via video **nasoendoscopy** (a scope watching the port during speech) that maps the gap pattern.

rows: Nasal tone on vowels and pressure sounds
Audible or mirror-fog leak on consonants

steps.say: The gap pattern seen on scopy is choosing the operation. Coronal patterns with a central gap are receiving a superiorly based posterior pharyngeal flap. Sagittal patterns with side gaps are receiving a sphincter pharyngoplasty instead. Matching the port shape is deciding success.
steps.tx: Surgical management of VPI matches the closure pattern: a superiorly based **posterior pharyngeal flap** (a back-wall bridge tethering the palate upward) suits **coronal** closure patterns (front to back wall motion with a central gap), while **sphincter pharyngoplasty** (a lateral narrowing ring) suits **sagittal** patterns (side-wall motion with lateral gaps). Scopy mapping precedes the choice.

steps.say: A hidden cleft is declaring itself through three small signs. Three small signs are defining it: a split uvula tip, a bony notch felt at the back of the hard palate, and a translucent midline zone where muscle is missing. Finding this triad is explaining hypernasality in a child with no open cleft.
steps.tx: **Submucous cleft palate** (a cleft hidden beneath intact mucosa) is defined by the classic **Calnan triad**: **bifid uvula** (a split uvula tip seen on oral inspection), a palpable posterior hard palate **notch** (a bony midline dip felt with a fingertip), and central muscular **diastasis** (separated levator bundles) visible as **zona pellucida** translucency. The triad explains nasal speech without an open gap.

vis.alt: Intraoral view of the soft palate and uvula for inspecting the Calnan triad of submucous cleft.
vis.caption: Palate and uvula on oral examination; a bifid uvula with a hard palate notch marks a submucous cleft. Credit: Wikipedia Medical (Uvula).
